name: Hillary Clinton
period: Secretary of state and presidential candidacy, 2009–2016
role: Former US secretary of state and 2016 presidential candidate
description: US political leader assessed through her foreign-policy record and 2016 presidential programme.

axes.brief: Competitive elections, universal adult suffrage, congressional accountability and independent courts underpin her institutional programme.
axes.counter: Representative constitutional politics does not establish endorsement of universal binding referendums or recall votes; these are qualified estimates.

axes.brief: Supported civil rights and judicial safeguards alongside intelligence surveillance and counterterrorism powers.
axes.counter: Gun restrictions, security interventions and the prosecution of classified leaks qualify a simple liberty label; exact modern policing cases require inference.

axes.brief: Celebrated a diverse American national community with minority inclusion and anti-discrimination measures.
axes.counter: Shared civic integration and national institutions remained important; distinct cultural expectations were not granted unlimited priority over common rights.

axes.brief: Favoured immigration reform, family unity, refugee protection and a pathway to citizenship for many undocumented residents.
axes.counter: Screening and lawful-entry enforcement remained; automatic permanent settlement or welfare eligibility for all noncitizens is broader than her programme.

axes.brief: Alliances, military capability and selective interventions including Libya accompanied diplomacy, arms-control negotiations and development.
axes.counter: Her 2016 speech defended the Iran agreement and cautioned against unnecessary war; force only after an attack and avoiding war at all costs are both too restrictive.

axes.brief: Strong alliances, international climate cooperation and trade rules were endorsed within continued US sovereignty.
axes.counter: Allied cooperation does not establish an international political federation, shared monetary authority or unconditional outside legal supremacy.

axes.brief: Regulated private enterprise, public services and infrastructure investment shaped her economic programme.
axes.counter: Public financing and a public insurance option do not mean most hospitals or competitive firms should be state-owned; national security retained mixed ownership.

axes.brief: Supported international commerce and opposed a trade war while seeking stronger labour protections and rejecting the proposed TPP in 2016.
axes.counter: Earlier promotion of trade negotiations and later opposition require a mixed period-specific estimate, rather than uniformly free-trade or protectionist answers.

axes.brief: Private production and market prices were normal, alongside minimum wages, industrial investment and financial regulation.
axes.counter: Infrastructure and clean-energy incentives steer development without compulsory economy-wide production targets; private competing currencies lack direct endorsement.

axes.brief: Proposed higher taxes on high earners, stronger income support, paid leave and help for low-paid workers.
axes.counter: A regulated market and targeted fiscal programme differed from equalising all incomes; compensated land redistribution is speculative and only weakly supported.

axes.brief: Civil government, plural religion and policy independent of clerical veto were supported.
axes.counter: Methodist belief, religious holidays and religious charitable exemptions were retained; these do not establish religious legislation as a foundation of the state.

axes.brief: Supported same-sex marriage by 2013, reproductive rights, women’s opportunities and LGBT equality in the scoped years.
axes.counter: Earlier marriage positions precede or sit early in this period; parental involvement and gradual institutional change qualify unbounded rejection of tradition.

axes.brief: Innovation, clean energy and infrastructure investment were priorities alongside environmental and biomedical safeguards.
axes.counter: Scientific investment alone cannot settle enhancement, cultivated meat or autonomous diagnosis; these are cautious question-specific analogies.

axes.brief: Federal constitutional states retained powers, with national civil-rights, education and healthcare goals.
axes.counter: No right of unilateral secession or unrestricted local obstruction follows; the national health programme was compatible with state delivery.

axes.brief: Educational access, discrimination and social barriers were central explanations for unequal opportunity.
axes.counter: This is contextual evidence for social influence, not a quoted claim that biology has no role in stress, temperament or cognition.
